files.summary: Reviewed all source/base lines, caller, tests and runtime configuration. Removing the reducer initializer breaks empty input.

findings.title: Restore the zero initializer for empty input
findings.problem: The changed reduce call omits its initial value, so total([]) throws TypeError instead of returning zero. The fixed base supplied 0.
findings.impact: The existing renderEmpty() caller now throws. Both direct and caller-level empty-input assertions in sum.test.ts require zero.
findings.recommendation: Restore items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item, 0). Retain the existing empty-input assertions.

report.summary: Review complete. No introduced regression found; one pre-existing precision defect remains. Tests were inspected, not run.

files.summary: Read full source and base, plus callers, tests and package metadata on both sides. Checked empty input and integer boundaries.

findings.title: Preserve precision across unsafe intermediate sums
findings.problem: Number accumulation can lose precision even when every input and the mathematical final sum are safe integers. For [Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 2, -2], the intermediate addition rounds, yielding 9007199254740990 instead of 9007199254740991. This defect also exists in the fixed base.
findings.impact: Inputs satisfying the documented contract can produce incorrect totals.
findings.recommendation: Accumulate using bigint and convert the safe final result to number. Add a regression test for [Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 2, -2].

anchorValidation.reason: Anchor matches a non-truncated source read. This does not prove the finding.

evidenceAssessment.rationale: Source reasoning under IEEE-754 arithmetic: the contract constrains inputs and final sum, but not intermediate totals. Adding the zero seed does not address this pre-existing limitation.
conditions: Safe-integer inputs produce an intermediate total that cannot be represented exactly.
Later cancellation brings the mathematical final sum back into the safe-integer range.

counterEvidence.summary: Existing tests cover empty input, small cancellation and a singleton maximum safe integer, but not cancellation after an inexact intermediate sum. The base has the same precision issue; this is not an introduced regression.
